meridian-credits/release-1.0-credit-agre: Meridian Credits release "1.0" credit agreement (Finance-approved, per issue trial-4tt). HISTORICAL: as of issue trial-a6r, release 1.0 is no longer the current agreement; an omitted release now selects "2.0" (see key meridian-credits/release-2.0-credit-agreement). Release 1.0 remains supported and is used only when a request sends explicit "release":"1.0". Rules: (1) uncapped line credit = 10% of charge_cents, floored per line to integer cents; (2) credit cap 2400 cents shared by all lines with the same account_id across its subscriptions, independent per account; (3) within a cap group, priority = earliest service_on first, ties by increasing line_id (Unicode code-point order); each line gets its uncapped credit up to the remaining cap, later lines get the remainder or zero; (4) total credit = sum of line credits; line amount_due = charge - credit; total due = total charges - total credit. Data model: line has exactly line_id, account_id, subscription_id, service_on (YYYY-MM-DD, 2020-01-01..2099-12-31), charge_cents (nonneg int); subscription key is (account_id, subscription_id); caps apply within one request. Quote command: {"command":"quote","line":LINE,"release":"1.0"} -> exactly {release, line_id, credit_cents, amount_due_cents}; single line is treated as the whole statement. Total command (issue trial-fjv): {"command":"total","lines":[LINE,...],"release":"1.0"} -> exactly {release, credit_cents, amount_due_cents}; caps apply across the whole supplied set, not per line; empty lines -> credit 0, due 0. Statement command (issue trial-8cl): {"command":"statement","lines":[LINE,...],"release":"1.0"} -> exactly {release, lines, credit_cents, amount_due_cents}, each response line exactly {line_id, credit_cents, amount_due_cents}, in input line order; uses release 1.0 cap scope and priority; totals equal total for the same input; empty lines -> {"release":"1.0","lines":[],"credit_cents":0,"amount_due_cents":0}. Implementation: main.py RELEASES["1.0"] entry (rate_percent 10, cap_cents 2400, cap_group account_id, priority (service_on, line_id)); assign_credits(lines, rules) runs the cap/priority engine; quote(), total() and statement() all call it. Public suites: python3 test_public.py --cases public_tests/release_1_quote.json, public_tests/release_1_total.json and public_tests/release_1_statement.json.
meridian-credits/release-2.0-credit-agre: Meridian Credits release "2.0" credit agreement (Finance-approved and permanently adopted as the CURRENT agreement, per issue trial-a6r; supersedes release 1.0 as current). Applies to every supplied charge set regardless of service dates. An omitted release now selects "2.0"; explicit "2.0" behaves identically; explicit "1.0" still uses the original agreement (see key meridian-credits/release-1.0-credit-agreement). Rules: (1) uncapped line credit = 15% of charge_cents, floored per line to integer cents; (2) credit cap 3000 cents shared by all lines with the same (account_id, subscription_id) pair; distinct pairs have independent caps (same subscription_id under different accounts = different groups); (3) within a cap group, priority = largest charge_cents first, ties by increasing line_id (Unicode code-point order); service_on never affects priority; each line gets its uncapped credit up to the remaining cap, later lines get the remainder or zero; (4) total credit = sum of line credits; line amount_due = charge - credit; total due = total charges - total credit. Request/response shapes unchanged from 1.0: quote {"command":"quote","line":LINE[,"release":R]} -> exactly {release, line_id, credit_cents, amount_due_cents}; total {"command":"total","lines":[LINE,...][,"release":R]} -> exactly {release, credit_cents, amount_due_cents}; the response release identifies the agreement actually used; unsupported release -> {"error":"unsupported_release"}. Example: quote L-1 charge 19999 with omitted release -> {"release":"2.0","credit_cents":2999,"amount_due_cents":17000,"line_id":"L-1"}. Statement command (added by issue trial-9mr): {"command":"statement","lines":[LINE,...][,"release":R]} -> exactly {release, lines, credit_cents, amount_due_cents}; each response line is exactly {line_id, credit_cents, amount_due_cents}; response lines preserve input order (not priority order); per-line credits come from the same cap-group/priority engine as total, so statement totals equal total for the same input; empty lines -> {"release":"2.0","lines":[],"credit_cents":0,"amount_due_cents":0}. Example: one line L-1 charge 19999 -> {"release":"2.0","credit_cents":2999,"amount_due_cents":17000,"lines":[{"line_id":"L-1","credit_cents":2999,"amount_due_cents":17000}]}. Implementation note (inference, not issue text): statement resolves release via the same resolve_release as quote/total, so explicit "1.0" itemizes under release 1.0 rules; the issue only specified omitted/"2.0". Implementation: main.py RELEASES table holds per-release rate_percent, cap_cents, cap_group key, and priority sort key; CURRENT_RELEASE = "2.0"; assign_credits(lines, rules) is the shared cap/priority engine used by quote(), total(), and statement(). Public suites: python3 test_public.py --cases public_tests/release_2_quote_total.json and public_tests/release_2_statement.json (release 1 suites remain applicable and must keep passing).
meridian-credits/support-case-fixtures: Meridian Credits support case fixtures (convention established in issue trial-wvr, case MC-406). A support case fixture is a one-off JSON file at support/<CASE-ID>.json (e.g. support/MC-406.json) containing exactly {"request": REQUEST, "response": RESPONSE}, where REQUEST is the complete request from the issue and RESPONSE is the CLI output produced by running python3 main.py with that request on stdin. Generate the response from the CLI rather than by hand. Public suites validate such fixtures with a case entry using "artifact_json_path" (test_public.py reads the file and compares it to "expected" with strict type/key equality), e.g. public_tests/case_MC_406.json. Fixtures do not change product commands or approved agreements.
